name: Swiss Poster
fit: Studios, architecture, serious portfolios, type-led sites
keywords: typography grid poster helvetica international swiss red
idea: The International Typographic Style: a strict 12-column grid, one grotesk, flush-left ragged-right text, a single red, and huge numerals doing the shouting.
note: Live: toggle the grid overlay to see how every element snaps to the 12 columns.
borrowed: Swiss posters by Josef Müller-Brockmann, Armin Hofmann and the Basel/Zürich schools: objective photography, mathematical grids, asymmetric layouts, Akzidenz/Helvetica, red and black on white.
mood: Rational, confident, timeless. Suits design studios, architecture, museums, serious portfolios, any type-led site that wants authority without decoration.

type.meta: Headings & body · Inter Tight 400–800 (stand-in for Akzidenz/Helvetica)

motion: Almost none. Content slides in along grid lines (translate by exactly one column).
A grid toggle is the one "toy": it shows the system behind the page.
Hover on links: underline thickens; nothing bounces.
watchouts: Easy to slide into generic minimalism. The huge numeral, the red and the visible grid are what make it Swiss.
Flush-left ragged-right only. Never justify or centre body text.
Use one family in two or three weights, no more.
